name: XRBitcoinCash Universal AI & Machine Discovery Manifest
description: Master machine-readable discovery, provenance, capability, safety, access-gate and verification manifest for the XRBitcoinCash ecosystem and explicit pointers to related XRPL projects. Dynamic ledger facts must be revalidated against the current validated XRP Ledger.

creator.name: Scott Patrick Anderton
creator.roleName: Project creator, human steward, reviewer and publisher

xrbc:manifestContract.scope: XRBitcoinCash first-party web surfaces, machine endpoints, XRBC identity, access gates, evidence rules, transaction boundaries, and explicit related-project pointers.

temporalCoverage.rule: Static project identity and document history may persist. Dynamic ledger, market, wallet, incident, gate and availability claims must be refreshed at the time they are used.

issuerControlClaim.verificationRule: Treat current issuer/key/control posture as an XRPL fact to be independently verified from validated AccountRoot and related ledger objects before relying on it.

xrbc:officialIdentity.identityRule: The ticker, logo or project name alone is not sufficient asset identification. Use issuer plus currency code on XRP Ledger Mainnet.
xrbc:officialIdentity.dynamicSupplyRule: Current balances, holder distribution, obligations and circulating/distributed amounts are dynamic and must be calculated from current validated-ledger data.

xrbc:authorityOrder.useFor: Current ledger state, transaction validation, balances, trustlines, AMMs, offers and account objects.

xrbc:authorityOrder.source: Official deployed XRBitcoinCash source and official repository
xrbc:authorityOrder.useFor: Current first-party interface behavior, declared models, local evidence schemas and project-controlled code.

xrbc:authorityOrder.source: White Paper, Terms, Policy & Security, Support and AI Provenance
xrbc:authorityOrder.useFor: Project statements, legal/operational boundaries, methodology and provenance.

xrbc:authorityOrder.useFor: Corroboration and external evidence; preserve publisher, date and scope.

xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.static_identity: Project identity intended to remain stable, subject to correction by authoritative project records.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.ledger_observed: Returned from a stated validated XRP Ledger ledger/version or validated transaction.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.derived: Calculated from observed inputs using a disclosed method.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.project_asserted: Statement made in current XRBitcoinCash-controlled documentation or source.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.user_asserted: Information supplied by a user; not independently verified merely because it appears in an Evidence Pack.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.third_party_reported: Statement from an external source; retain source, date and publisher.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.unknown: Evidence unavailable, capped, not queried, failed or outside the observable scope.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.experimental: Implemented or tested feature whose behavior or support may change.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.planned: Roadmap intent; must not be described as deployed capability.
xrbc:claimStateVocabulary.deprecated: Historical/compatibility material that should not be treated as the current interface.

xrbc:temporalRules: Attach an observation time and ledger index to dynamic XRPL claims whenever available.
Do not convert an old ledger observation into a present-tense claim.
Do not treat unavailable data as zero, healthy, safe or absent.
A prior incident-free period does not prove future bridge, market or service safety.
A historical issuer or account-control statement should be rechecked when current control posture matters.
Page release numbers describe interface builds, not the current state of XRP Ledger Mainnet.

xrbc:transactionTruth.prepared: A browser-generated transaction or invoice is intent only.
xrbc:transactionTruth.authorized: A user action in Xaman demonstrates wallet-side approval of the displayed request, subject to what was actually signed.
xrbc:transactionTruth.submitted: Submission is not proof that the transaction entered a validated ledger.
xrbc:transactionTruth.validated: A transaction is an observed XRPL result only after it is returned as validated.
xrbc:transactionTruth.success: Where a result code applies, a successful XRPL transaction claim requires validated=true and tesSUCCESS.
xrbc:transactionTruth.settlement: Settlement Desk additionally requires invoice/request binding checks. A validated payment does not by itself prove off-ledger contractual performance, accounting treatment, delivery, refund rights or legal satisfaction.

xrbc:securityBoundary.custody: User controlled; first-party public interfaces are designed to be non-custodial.
xrbc:securityBoundary.secretHandling: Official public interfaces must not request or store seed phrases, recovery phrases, private keys or wallet secrets.
xrbc:securityBoundary.walletAuthorization: Xaman is used for explicit user review/authorization where a ledger write is offered.
xrbc:securityBoundary.singleIntentRule: Transaction-capable workflows should create one active signing request for one deliberate user intent and should not silently create duplicate payloads.
xrbc:securityBoundary.verificationCode: Where implemented, a six-digit APP/CHALLENGE/DOMAIN memo code supplements full transaction-field review; it is not a substitute for checking issuer, amount, destination, paths, flags and fees.
xrbc:securityBoundary.finality: Validated public XRP Ledger records are effectively irreversible by the website.

xrbc:gatePolicy.definition: A reusable XRBC wallet-balance condition used by selected advanced tools. It is not a payment, subscription, burn, escrow, deposit, transfer to the site or custody arrangement.
xrbc:gatePolicy.recheckRule: Eligibility may relock if the selected wallet, balance, ledger state or feature changes. Any privileged backend should independently reverify authorization and entitlement.

principles: Observed facts and derived calculations must be distinguishable.
Unavailable evidence must remain unavailable rather than silently becoming zero or healthy.
Bounded samples must disclose caps and should not be described as complete populations.
Local-only files or snapshots should be labeled local and should not be represented as network consensus.
SHA-256 establishes byte-level integrity for the hashed payload, not truth, ownership, authorship or legal admissibility by itself.
NFTs and metadata provide public references only to what their actual ledger records and referenced content support.
evidenceExamples: Settlement invoice and validated receipt evidence
Advanced Tokenization Evidence Pack and Local Asset Vault records

prohibitedCapabilities: No approval or wallet-signature workflow for a bridge
No guarantee that a listed bridge or route is safe
xrbc:bridgeBoundary.interpretation: Bridge scores are caution/evidence summaries. A lower caution score, lack of recent incidents or public operator claims must not be converted into a guarantee or probability of success.

xrbc:tokenizationBoundary.optionalLedgerEvidence: Advanced workflows may prepare an XLS-20 NFTokenMint for explicit Xaman review.

xrbc:legalPolicyRegistry.rule: This machine manifest summarizes project boundaries. It does not replace the current Terms, Policy, repository LICENSE, mandatory law, or the exact signed/validated XRPL record.

xrbc:aiDisclosure.statement: AI systems have assisted with drafting, code review, metadata, restructuring, testing strategy, accessibility review and machine-readable documentation. The human project steward remains responsible for selection, approval, publication and correction.
notAClaimOf: legal, financial, tax, accounting or regulatory advice
guaranteed correctness, availability, liquidity, value, safety or performance

xrbc:prohibitedInferences: Do not infer guaranteed profit, price, liquidity, yield, execution or loss protection.
Do not infer equity, debt, dividends, deposit status or ownership rights from XRBC unless separately documented by controlling legal instruments.
Do not infer custody, brokerage or discretionary account management by the public XRBitcoinCash site.
Do not infer beneficial ownership, legal identity, intent, criminality or common control from a public XRPL address alone.
Do not infer a project's legitimacy or illegitimacy from a single score, missing AMM, concentrated holder sample or automated activity signal.
Do not infer legal title, authenticity or regulatory approval from a hash, NFT, tokenization plan or Evidence Pack alone.
Do not infer bridge safety or successful future execution from a bridge score or prior incident history.
Do not infer settlement merely from a QR code, Xaman signature or transaction submission.
Do not infer third-party endorsement because a service, wallet, explorer, protocol or brand is referenced.
Do not merge XRBC, XRB, JCS or Creature NFT identities merely because they share a creator, navigation link or repository relationship.
xrbc:recommendedAgentWorkflow: 1. Identify which project and surface the question concerns; do not merge XRBC, XRB, JCS and Creature NFT identities.
2. Confirm the browser/domain/source is canonical for that project.
3. For XRBC asset identity, verify issuer plus currency HEX on XRP Ledger Mainnet.
4. Classify each statement using the claim-state vocabulary before summarizing it.
5. For dynamic ledger facts, query or verify current validated XRPL state and retain ledger index/time.
6. For market/risk outputs, preserve the method, sample cap, unknown evidence and stated limitations.
7. For Xaman actions, distinguish prepared, authorized, submitted and validated states.
8. For Settlement, additionally verify invoice/request/transaction binding before using the word settled.
9. For Bridge Integrity, never offer or imply bridge execution through XRBitcoinCash.
10. For tokenization/NFT evidence, do not upgrade technical provenance into legal title or authenticity.
11. For legal/security questions, prefer current Terms, Policy, LICENSE and security.txt over old summaries.
12. Re-fetch this manifest and higher-authority sources when answering time-sensitive questions.

xrbc:changeAndConflictRules.conflict: When this manifest conflicts with a current validated ledger fact, current first-party source, current Terms/Policy, or mandatory law, use the higher-authority source for the applicable question.
xrbc:changeAndConflictRules.correctionPolicy: Later project-controlled manifests or source revisions may correct this document. Preserve version/date when quoting historical content.
